name: Distance to the Path
description: You are given a tree consisting of $$$n$$$ vertices. Initially, each vertex has a value $$$0$$$. You need to perform $$$m$$$ queries of two types: You are given a vertex index $$$v$$$. Print the value of the vertex $$$v$$$. You are given two vertex indices $$$u$$$ and $$$v$$$ and values $$$k$$$ and $$$d$$$ ($$$d \le 20$$$). You need to add $$$k$$$ to the value of each vertex such that the distance from that vertex to the path from $$$u$$$ to $$$v$$$ is less than or equal to $$$d$$$. The distance between two vertices $$$x$$$ and $$$y$$$ is equal to the number of edges on the path from $$$x$$$ to $$$y$$$. For example, the distance from $$$x$$$ to $$$x$$$ itself is equal to $$$0$$$. The distance from the vertex $$$v$$$ to some path from $$$x$$$ to $$$y$$$ is equal to the minimum among distances from $$$v$$$ to any vertex on the path from $$$x$$$ to $$$y$$$.
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$n$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the number of vertices in the tree. Next $$$n - 1$$$ lines contain the edges of the tree — one per line. Each line contains two integers $$$u$$$ and $$$v$$$ ($$$1 \le u, v \le n$$$; $$$u \neq v$$$) representing one edge of the tree. It's guaranteed that the given edges form a tree. The next line contains a single integer $$$m$$$ ($$$1 \le m \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the number of queries. Next $$$m$$$ lines contain the queries — one per line. Each query has one of the following two types: $$$1$$$ $$$v$$$ ($$$1 \le v \le n$$$) — the query of the first type; $$$2$$$ $$$u$$$ $$$v$$$ $$$k$$$ $$$d$$$ ($$$1 \le u, v \le n$$$; $$$1 \le k \le 1000$$$; $$$0 \le d \le 20$$$) — the query of the second type. Additional constraint on the input: there is at least one query of the first type.
output_specification: For each query of the first type, print the value of the corresponding vertex.
approach_summary: Build a Segment Tree over the array. Implement point update and associative range query operations in O(log N) time per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1749F — Distance to the Path [57. Segment Tree (Point Update Range Query)]
topic_editorial.summary: Range queries and updates via Segment Tree.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The query operation is associative (e.g., sum, min, max, gcd). Any contiguous range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into at most $O(\log N)$ canonical dyadic intervals represented by nodes in a binary tree.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Tree Construction
We build a binary segment tree over array $A[1..N]$.
Each node covers a segment $[L, R]$. If $L = R$, the node stores $A[L]$. Otherwise:
$$\text{node.val} = \text{combine}(\text{left\_child.val}, \text{right\_child.val})$$

### Step 2: Point / Range Updates
To update position $pos$ with value $val$:
- Traverse down to the leaf node $[pos, pos]$.
- Update leaf value.
- Recompute ancestor values on the way back up in $O(\log N)$ time.

### Step 3: Range Query Processing
To query the associative aggregate on range $[qL, qR]$:
- If current segment $[L, R]$ is completely within $[qL, qR]$, return node value.
- If disjoint, return identity element.
- Otherwise, split and return $\text{combine}(\text{query}(left), \text{query}(right))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}((N + Q) \log N)$
  Building the segment tree takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$. Each point/range query and update traverses at most $4 \log N$ tree nodes, requiring $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ time per query.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  A standard binary segment tree requires at most $4N$ nodes to represent elements up to index $N$.
